Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

controlcompR 0.1.0

  • First version.
    • Models: continuous and discrete state-space, transfer-function, zero-pole-gain and static gain models with MIMO support and signal names; conversions; zero-order hold, first-order hold, Tustin and matched discretization and ctrl_d2c().
    • Interconnections: series, parallel, feedback with well-posedness checks, block diagrams by signal name, closed loops, sensitivity functions and linear fractional transformations.
    • Analysis: poles, transmission zeros, damping, stability with explicit tolerances, staircase controllability and observability, Gramians, minimal realizations, stable and unstable decomposition.
    • Matrix equations: Lyapunov, Stein and Sylvester solvers; continuous and discrete Riccati solvers based on ordered Schur forms, with residual and stability verification.
    • Time and frequency responses, step metrics, gain, phase, delay and disk margins, bandwidth, H2 and H-infinity norms, root locus.
    • Design: LQR (continuous, discrete, finite horizon), robust pole placement, observers, Kalman filters and the RTS smoother, LQG, PID controllers with filters, anti-windup and bumpless transfer, tuning rules.
    • Linear MPC with OSQP: input, rate, state, output and terminal constraints, soft constraints, offset-free tracking and explicit failure handling; moving horizon estimation with warm starts.
    • Robust control: H2 synthesis and experimental, certified H-infinity synthesis for continuous time with D11 = 0; mixed-sensitivity plants; robust stability and robust performance tests for unstructured uncertainty.
    • Model reduction by balanced truncation and residualization.
    • System identification: ARX, order selection, subspace identification, validation tools and conversion of sysid models.
    • Nonlinear systems: simulation, linearization, equilibria, discretization, EKF, UKF, experimental nonlinear MPC with adjoint gradients and trajectory optimization with terminal constraints.
    • Fifteen articles and a reference comparison against python-control and SLICOT.
  • Numerical contracts worth knowing:
    • Gramian factors for Hankel singular values, balanced realization, balanced truncation and the H2 norm are computed directly with Hammarling’s method, so the Gramians are never formed and rotated or badly scaled realizations keep their weak directions.
    • Balanced truncation checks its error bound on a frequency sample and against the error system’s H-infinity norm, stops with an error when its samples contradict the bound, and reports bound_status ("certified" or "estimated") and error_norm. ctrl_balreal() runs the same check on the removed states.
    • Stability is decided on a realization balanced together with B and C, without a fixed unit floor in continuous time, and with per-pole bands from the first-order eigenvalue error bound (pole_tol).
    • Covariances are inverted on their support after scaling to unit diagonal in the UKF update, the RTS smoother and the MHE arrival cost; a positive direction is kept unless its equilibrated variance is at the rounding level (10 n eps), also when it is rotated away from the axes. The MHE QP is solved in the prior’s own coordinates scaled to unit curvature.
    • Positive definiteness of weights and covariances is decided after scaling to unit diagonal, so it does not depend on units.
    • State-space frequency responses solve the resolvent without a condition-number cutoff, so badly scaled but nonsingular realizations are evaluated; only singular or overflowing solves give NA.
    • Loop internal stability checks use the same policy as ctrl_stability().
    • Design functions (LQR, pole placement, Kalman design, offset-free MPC, H2 and H-infinity synthesis) and the ctrl_is_*() predicates use only the staircase reduction; the PBH table and controllability matrix singular values are computed only by ctrl_controllability() and ctrl_observability(). LQR on a 120-state model is about three times faster.
    • The native LAPACK wrappers check argument types, dimensions, modes and tolerances at entry, check workspace queries before using their sizes, stop on invalid-argument codes and accept empty matrices. The test suite runs clean under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, and a CI workflow repeats that on every push.
  • Performance:
    • Discrete Lyapunov equations solve the triangular Stein equation in native code (about five times faster at 120 states).
    • Frequency responses on many points use one complex Schur factorization and triangular solves (about six times faster at 120 states); short point lists keep the dense solve.
    • The controllability staircase transforms only the trailing blocks; QZ computes only the Schur vectors the caller needs.
    • MPC and MHE assemble their QPs from chunked triplets in linear time; MHE reuses the OSQP workspace while the QP sparsity is unchanged and advances the prior covariance lazily instead of storing one per sample.
    • ARX order selection builds the lagged regressors once (about five times faster); ARX prediction is vectorized and N4SID validation does not simulate twice.
    • The LQG simulation factors its constant algebraic loop once.
    • NMPC shares each prediction between the cost and the gradient, and ctrl_nlsys() accepts analytic Jacobians (jacobian), used by linearization, the EKF and NMPC instead of finite differences.
    • ctrl_kalman_filter(), ctrl_ekf() and ctrl_ukf() accept covariances = "variances" to store only the filtered variances.
    • ctrl_mpc() and ctrl_mhe() accept accuracy = "high" (default), "standard" or "fast" solver profiles; the MPC article measures the trade-off.
    • Robust stability decisions and H-infinity synthesis certification use the upper bound of the norm computation (upper_bound); an attained zero H-infinity optimum is returned with gamma = 0.
    • ctrl_robust_performance() samples its peaks (including zero and infinite frequency) and reports a separate certified flag from a rigorous upper bound; the SISO exactness flag is criterion_exact.
    • Nyquist encirclement counts come from the argument principle (unstable closed-loop minus open-loop roots) and are NA when a closed-loop pole lies on the stability boundary or 1 + D = 0.
    • ctrl_zeros() stops with an error for systems whose pencil is singular (no full normal rank), decided by evaluating the transfer matrix away from every computed eigenvalue and pole. With a well-conditioned D, zeros too large for the pencil to separate from infinity are taken from A - B D^-1 C; otherwise an eigenvalue that cannot be told apart from infinity gives a warning.
    • Step, impulse and initial responses are applied at time zero; grids that start later report the same response at their own instants.
    • ctrl_step_info() reports final_value_known separately from settled, which is now always based on the simulated horizon.
    • ctrl_pid_update() has init = "hold" (default) and init = "zero" (zero history, matching the zero-state response of ctrl_pid_tf()).
    • EKF and UKF results have class ctrl_nl_filter and are not accepted by ctrl_kalman_smoother(); infinite measurements are rejected (only NA marks missing data).
    • NMPC simulation needs a discrete plant with the controller’s sample interval; the "hold" fallback is clipped to the input bounds and the first held input is set by u0.
    • Numeric scalars scale every channel of MIMO models; dividing a model by a square numeric matrix multiplies by its inverse on the input side.
    • Riccati solvers equilibrate the equation (weight scale, state units, time scale and input units) before solving, so solutions are invariant to the units of states, inputs, costs and time; the reported residual is that of the equilibrated equation.
    • The Kalman filter, EKF, UKF and MHE reject non-numeric data and rows that are only partly missing; an entirely NA row is a missing sample.
    • Fast or slow SISO transfer functions are realized with scaled states when the scaled coefficients stay representable; otherwise the unscaled companion form is used.
    • Matched discretization treats a root as an origin root only when it is negligible both against the other roots and against the sample interval.
    • The PID loop through plant feedthrough uses the exact affine slope of the controller output.
    • Scalar model arithmetic that overflows, nonfinite Kalman prior means and negative NMPC penalties are rejected.
    • Static loops adopt the clock of a discrete weight in ctrl_robust_performance(); synthesis rank checks on D12 and D21 are relative to each block.
